conviction_note: A modest up-lean: an independent traffic series (Placer.ai Q3 same-store visits +12.3%) and Ross's own record of beating its comp guide by 3-10 points point to another Q3 beat. Q4 guidance decides the print. TJX's documents flag three things that can cap a raise: warm weather in early November, diesel running above the price Ross built into its August guide, and Marmaxx matching competitors' price cuts. The skew already pays for upside, and the whisper ($1.91) sits above the top of the guide, so p_up 57 on a 7.5% abs move gives +1.05, close to the findings' sum of +1.0.
bar: Company Q3 guide: comps +6-7%, total sales +9-11%, EPS $1.75-1.83, operating margin 11.7-12.0% (Q2 release https://finviz.com/news/384306/ross-stores-reports-strong-second-quarter-sales-and-earnings-results and Q2 call https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-2038385-20260828). Street EPS: $1.82 on ~$6.20B revenue with a $1.91 whisper (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-11, https://finviz.com/news/421342/ross-stores-faces-a-higher-bar-as-the-whisper-sits-above-its-own-third-quarter-guidance); the sweep carries $1.85 from 7 estimates. The two estimate sources differ by 3 cents and both sit at or above the top of the company guide. Q4 guide in hand: comps +4-5% lapping +9%, EPS $2.17-2.26. No sourced Q4 consensus was found. print_vs_bar is on revenue: a ~9% comp would make total sales ~+12-13%, about $6.3B against $6.20B.
positioning_check: Short interest about 9.8M shares and 4.6 days to cover as of 2026-11-04, falling (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/rost/shortinterest). Other trackers give ~10.2M shares, about 3.0-3.3% of float, and 4.4-5.9 days to cover (https://fintel.io/ss/us/rost, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=ROST). Not a crowded short. Baseline 25d skew is -13.9 vol points (calls bid, 'upside paid'), but put/call open interest is 3.0. The straddle implies 7.19%, against a median 8.03% on 7 prior prints, 6 of them up. Tape: ROST closed $241.27 on Nov 11 and $220.45 on Nov 17 (-8.6%) while SPY went from 759.8 to 732.4 (-3.6%). On Nov 18 ROST rose only +3.3%, against TJX +8.0% and BURL +5.5% on TJX's print. Today ROST is -1.5% intraday with SPY -1.3% (Yahoo chart, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ROST?range=1mo&interval=1d).

findings.finding: Placer.ai puts Ross Q3 2026 same-store visits at +12.3% YoY, 'near or above 10% in every month through October'. Ross guided Q3 comps to only +6-7%. The same tracker read +16.4% visits in Q2, when Ross printed a 10% traffic-led comp against a 6-7% guide, and Ross printed +17% in Q1. EPS guide tops were also beaten in both quarters: Q2 ex-refund ~$2.06 vs a $1.85-1.93 guide, Q1 $2.02 vs $1.60-1.67. The comp likely lands near 8-10%. At Ross's stated 10-15 bps of margin per comp point, that is EPS ~$1.88-1.93 against the $1.82-1.85 consensus and the $1.91 whisper.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ross has been paid for comp beats. Q2 2026 (10% vs 6-7%) +4.39%, Q1 2026 (17%) +8.11%, Q4 2025 +8.03%, Q3 2025 +8.41%. The one large drop (2025-05-22, -9.85%) came on the outlook, not the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the $1.91 whisper sits above the guide top and calls are bid. If the market fully held a ~9% comp, consensus would sit near the whisper, not at the guide top ($1.82). The stock would not have fallen 8.6% from Nov 11 to Nov 17, more than twice SPY's -3.6%, or lagged TJX's and BURL's rebound on Nov 18.
findings.independence: Company documents for the beat history: Q2 release https://finviz.com/news/384306/ross-stores-reports-strong-second-quarter-sales-and-earnings-results and Q1 release https://finviz.com/news/356461/ross-stores-reports-robust-first-quarter-sales-and-earnings-results-significantly-exceeding-guidance. The Placer series itself is a single third-party proxy.

findings.finding: TJX's Q3 FY27 release and call (2026-11-18) show Marmaxx, Ross's most direct competitor, at a 2% comp with 'customer transactions essentially flat', growth coming from basket only. TJX said 'some competition has lowered' prices and Marmaxx matched. Placer separately has Marshalls same-store visits 'roughly flat'. Ross's comps have been traffic-led, so the peer document supports continued traffic share gains for Ross. It also confirms price competition, which could pressure merchandise margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Aug 2026, TJX's Marmaxx miss (1% comp) was followed by ROST +4.39% on its own beat. On 2026-11-18, TJX's beat lifted ROST only +3.3%, against TJX +8.0% and BURL +5.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer printed one day before Ross. Sell-side Ross estimates (consensus at the guide top) have not visibly moved on it. ROST's muted +3.3% on Nov 18 suggests the market read TJX as a TJX-specific recovery, not as confirmation of Ross's share gains.
findings.independence: Placer.ai (2026-11-16) has Marshalls same-store visits roughly flat and T.J. Maxx turning positive only in September: https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/off-price-on-course-ross-and-tjx-in-q3-2026 (this shares a source with finding 1, on a different chain). TJX 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm

findings.finding: Ross does not hedge fuel. Its August guide assumed 'current higher fuel prices', with EIA diesel at $5.454/gal in the week of Aug 17. Diesel then ran above $6 from early September and only fell back to $5.9989 (AAA) on Nov 16; EIA read $6.127 for the week of Nov 9. So Q3 domestic freight ran roughly 10-12% above the fuel price in the guide and Q4 is still above it. TJX cut its own Q4 outlook for 'additional fuel costs' and called fuel and freight its largest Q4 headwind (Q4 gross margin -50-60 bps). My estimate is ~10-20 bps on Ross's Q3 margin (~$0.02-0.03 EPS) and a reason to hold rather than raise Q4 EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Ross print turned on freight. TJX's own Q4 fuel cut did not stop TJX rising 11% on 2026-11-18.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at the guide top and a $1.91 whisper suggest nobody has marked down Ross's freight. If they had, the whisper would sit inside the guide range. The fuel arithmetic needs the August assumption from the call, the EIA series and TJX's Q4 comment combined, and no preview found does that.
findings.independence: Diesel series: FRED/EIA $5.454 for Aug 17 (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/?g=1XTvU) and $6.127 for Nov 9; AAA <$6 for the first time since early September (https://stockanalysis.com/news/us-diesel-falls-below-6-gallon/). TJX Q4 fuel cut: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm. Against it: Oxford expects fuel to ease in November (https://www.zerohedge.com/markets/equity-weakness-continues-nvda-earnings-await-newsquawk-us-market-wrap).

findings.finding: TJX's CEO said on 2026-11-18 that 'unseasonably warm weather in the U.S. and Canada has been holding back consumer demand in some categories so far' in the holiday quarter. That overlaps Ross's Q4 (Nov-Jan), for which Ross guided comps +4-5% lapping +9%. It makes a Q4 comp raise, or upbeat November quarter-to-date commentary, from Ross less likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ross's only large negative reaction (2025-05-22, -9.85%) was on the outlook. Raised outlooks were bought (+4.4% to +8.4%).
findings.why_not_priced: TJX rose 11% on the same call, so the market treated the weather comment as noise for TJX. A Q4 raise from Ross would be a fourth straight one, which Earnings Whispers calls 'plausible'. If the weather drag were priced, the skew would not be call-bid into the print.
findings.independence: Proxy, not confirmed by Ross. October Census clothing-store sales fell ~0.7% m/m, the biggest drop since January (finding 5, https://stockanalysis.com/news/us-retail-sales-rise-october-2026/). TJX itself also expects momentum to 'accelerate throughout the holiday selling season', which cuts against this finding and is reflected in its small size.

findings.finding: The October 2026 Census advance report shows clothing and accessories store sales down about 0.7% m/m, against headline retail +0.2% and control group +0.6%. October is the last month of Ross's Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of ROST reacting to Census apparel data on its prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Released on 2026-11-17 and probably priced by now. It is an industry proxy, and the company-level Placer series (finding 1) contradicts it for Ross, so it is sized below that series.
findings.independence: Same data reported at https://www.wcax.com/2026/11/17/spending-growth-slowed-retail-stores-october-high-prices-give-shoppers-pause/ (same Census release, not independent).

findings.finding: The pre-print drawdown is mostly market and relative-beta, not company-specific. ROST fell from $241.27 (Nov 11) to $220.45 (Nov 17) as SPY fell 759.8 to 732.4 on an AI-led selloff. It then lagged the off-price rebound on Nov 18: ROST +3.3%, TJX +8.0%, BURL +5.5%. The stock goes into the print 12.5% below its 52-week high, with a lower bar than a week ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last two prints from different setups: Aug 2026 +4.39% after TJX's Marmaxx miss the day before; May 2026 +8.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information; the price is the measurement. It is small because a market-wide selloff (SPY -5% from Nov 11) can continue through the window.

baseline_tension: The up-lean agrees with the call-bid skew (-13.9) and Ross's up-reaction history, so it is partly priced. The negative 20-day run-up (-5.7%) and the lag behind peers on Nov 18 leave room above it; the guidance-line negatives cut against the skew.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy vs company series, documents beat inference): fuel finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7 because it is arithmetic from a series, not a Ross number; warm-weather finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6 as unconfirmed macro transmission; Census apparel cut from -0.3 to -0.2 because the company-level Placer series contradicts it
Lesson 1 (reaction function): Ross has paid for comp beats in 6 of 7 prints, so finding 1 left at +1.5
Lesson 6 (bar): bar is sourced to the company guide plus two estimate sources ($1.82/$1.85) that roughly agree, so no cap applied
Lesson 3: TJX's own 'momentum will accelerate' caveat on the weather finding is reflected in its size; finding 2 trimmed from +0.7 to +0.6 because it also confirms price competition
Lesson 7: short interest checked (~3% of float, 4.6 days to cover, not crowded), so no shrink of the negatives for squeeze risk; the positioning finding trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3
